function: Learns the location-to-channel mapping (channel synthesis and prediction at any location, and radio-environment compression) for a multi-antenna, multi-frequency BS from ray-traced channel samples (pp. 4, 9-11).
system: BS with ULA (up to 64 antennas) and up to 64 frequencies, single-antenna UEs; 3.5 GHz, 50 MHz, 10 m by 10 m scene; no RIS (pp. 3, 7-8).
method: Model-based hypernetwork derived from a Taylor-expanded ray channel model: complex Fourier-feature layer plus MLPs learning dictionaries and sparse weights; supervised training with Frobenius loss (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Sionna ray tracing: Etoile scene in Paris (D1, D2 without LoS) and empty scene (D3); 17.5k random training locations, about 210k grid test locations (pp. 8-9).
test_conditions: Train on random locations, test on a dense lambda/4 grid of the same scene; frequency generalization: train 32 frequencies, test 64; training density and compression sweeps (pp. 8-9).
baselines: Learned only: complex MLP and complex RFF networks (Gaussian-drawn, or model-based circle-sampled spatial frequencies); no non-learned baseline (pp. 8-9).
metrics: NMSE in dB over the test grid, versus training density, frequency and antenna index, Ns, Na, and compression ratio (pp. 8-12).
complexity: Parameter counts: MLP 10.5M, RFF 669k, model-based variants 9.1M and 851k (Table I); no FLOPs or runtime figure (pp. 9, 11).
openness: none (Sionna is a third-party open-source library; no link to the authors' code or datasets) (p. 14).
q1_support: p. 8: "Realistic synthetic channels are generated using the Sionna ray-tracing library". Ray tracing in the public Etoile scene (D1, D2) and an empty scene (D3); no 3GPP model or measured data, so another public ray-tracing source, reviewer to confirm.
q2_support: p. 9: "trained on the D1 dataset with Ns = 32, and evaluated on Ns = 64 frequencies". The test includes frequencies unseen in training, where the NMSE is higher but stays low.
q3_support: p. 9: "1. is a classical complex MLP while 2. and 3. are complex RFFs". All baselines are learned networks; ray tracing (p. 8) and sparse recovery (p. 6) are only discussed, never compared on NMSE, so no non-learned baseline.
q4_support: p. 11: "the 9.1M learning parameters of the MB". About 9.1 million parameters for the main model-based network (D = 1000); Table I (p. 9) lists parameters of every model; no FLOPs or runtime.
q5_support: p. 8: "Three different datasets are considered". The authors generate these datasets themselves; no link or DOI to their code or data appears, and the only open resource cited is the third-party Sionna library (p. 14).
notes: q1 is marked met because the channels come from Sionna ray tracing in the public Etoile scene (D1, D2) and an empty scene (D3), another public ray-tracing source rather than 3GPP or DeepMIMO; reviewer to confirm. q2 rests on the frequency generalization test (train Ns = 32, test Ns = 64). q3 is 0 because every compared model is learned. q5 is 0 because the datasets are generated by the authors with the public Sionna tool and scene but are not released; reviewer to confirm. Included as area 2 (channel synthesis, prediction, compression); the paper says it does not target precise channel estimation (p. 12). Preprint (arXiv v3).
